00.summary: Foreword items are listed but not counted, because the chapters cover the same ground. Of 21 Foreword records, four are in effect: DEI and gender-term removal, international withdrawals, border enforcement and energy. Thirteen are underway, two diverged (China economic engagement and the TikTok ban) and two are proposed (pornography and children's social media). Five records added 2026-10-14 restate chapter objectives on the military, the civil service, education alternatives and executive mandates, and take their stage from the detailed records.

01.summary: Two of nine tracked recommendations are in effect: since 2025-02-25 the White House selects the press pool, and the Counsel reviewed pending litigation. A district court preliminary injunction of 2026-10-13 ordered the hard passes of three outlets restored and the government noticed an appeal on 2026-10-14; the Associated Press appeal argued 2025-11-24 has no decision. Three are underway (policy-council roles, Presidential Personnel Office clearance and NSC staffing under NSPM-1), the DOJ contacts policy rests on the 2021 memorandum still in the Justice Manual, two show no action and one diverged.

02.summary: Eleven of 20 tracked recommendations are in effect, resting on OMB's apportionment delegation (effective 2025-02-11), EO 14215 on OIRA review of independent agencies, CEQ's removal of its NEPA regulations, EO 14168, EO 14148, EO 14192 and EO 14303, under which DOE, EPA, Interior, Commerce and NSF issued revised scientific integrity policies between 2025-07-24 and 2026-09-01. Five are underway, including NSC reorganization under NSPM-1 and a proposed amendment to the Fifth National Climate Assessment. Two rest on proposals; no action was found on OMB's resource management offices or OIRA staffing.

03.summary: Five of nine objectives are in effect: Schedule Policy/Career (EO 14171 and EO 14410; OPM rule effective 2026-03-09), limits on union bargaining (EO 14251, EO 14343), merit hiring (EO 14170), workforce controls (EO 14210; OPM reduction-in-force rule effective 2026-09-02) and Schedule G (EO 14317). Appraisal and removal changes are underway, with OPM's probationary appeals rule effective 2026-09-02 and an MSPB penalty-review rule effective 2026-10-05, while pay and retirement legislation was not enacted. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB is classed as diverged. Union litigation continues: a First Circuit panel stayed a VA contract-extension order about 2026-10-02, and a Connecticut court ordered Bureau of Prisons agreements restored in late September 2026.

04.summary: Five of 31 objectives are in effect: EO 14183 on transgender service (a certiorari petition in Talbott is pending), EO 14184 reinstatements, EO 14185 on DEI offices, the end of abortion travel funding and the cut in critical technology areas. Twenty are underway, among them acquisition reform (EO 14265), Golden Dome (EO 14186), about 41 billion dollars of munitions funding under P.L. 119-21 and the Fourth Circuit stay of 2026-06-25 in the HIV accession case. Four diverged, including the 2026 defense strategy's one-war-plus construct and the NSA and Cyber Command dual hat.

05.summary: Eight of 35 tracked recommendations are in effect: nationwide expedited removal, detention and ICE funding (P.L. 119-21, P.L. 119-98), ended parole and TPS programs, 287(g) growth, the final public charge rule, a replaced advisory council and EOIR's end of administrative closure. Sixteen are underway, among them wall funding and sanctions on countries refusing deportees, where an EOIR rule of 2025-08-28 allows temporary immigration judges while the permanent judge count fell to 557 by the end of 2025. Eight rest on proposals, two items are blocked and one is diverged.

06.summary: Eleven of 27 tracked recommendations are in effect, including all seven key objectives (refugee suspension, with the FY2027 determination of 2026-09-25 allowing up to 17,500 admissions, the 2026-01-07 withdrawal memorandum, the State reorganization, entry proclamations and the aid pause). Ten are underway, among them the Venezuela campaign (EO 14245, the 2025-11-16 cartel designation and the 2026-01-03 capture of Maduro), Red Sea and Gulf operations, Africa commercial diplomacy and Quad engagement, while relations with Pakistan run opposite to the text. Five rest on proposals, including a China strategy paper and cyber norms; no action was found on Circular 175 authorities.

07.summary: One of 21 tracked recommendations is in effect: ODNI was restructured from 2025-08-20 with staff reductions. Six are underway, including clearance revocations and leak policy changes under EO 14152, CIA workforce changes and post-quantum orders. FISA Section 702 lapsed on 2026-06-12 and is classed as blocked. Nine rest on proposals, among them classification reform, the advisory board tasking and space integration, where EO 14369 of 2025-12-18 directs plans only. No public action was found on EO 14086, a covert action review or 48-hour cyber sharing.

08.summary: Two of six tracked recommendations are in effect: the Rescissions Act of 2025 (P.L. 119-28, signed 2025-07-24) cancelled about $1.1 billion for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and acting leadership was installed at USAGM, although a 2026-03-07 court ruling voided one official's acting-CEO actions. Two are underway: EO 14238 (2025-03-14) directed USAGM reduced to its statutory minimum while Congress enacted about $652.7 million for FY2026. The NCE-status objective remains a proposal, and no journalist safety measures were found.

09.summary: Seven of twenty tracked recommendations are in effect, among them foreign assistance placed under State with USAID wound down by 2025-07-01, aid reductions (P.L. 119-28), rules on gender, equity and abortion terms (effective 2026-02-26), an AGOA extension and appointee review of awards under EO 14332. Seven are underway, including humanitarian aid and global health compacts. Three rest on proposals: DFC reauthorization in P.L. 119-60 runs parallel to the text, and religious freedom and Pacific aid rest on summaries and announcements. The WHO withdrawal is diverged; no action was found on section 653(a) reporting or the moot USAID staffing plan.

10.summary: Two of 17 tracked recommendations are in effect: SNAP changes in P.L. 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) and the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines. Four are underway, including forest management and biotechnology review changes, and five rest on bills or early steps, among them checkoff reform, where a USDA directive of 2026-09-17 ended dairy checkoff funding of ESG projects. Four are classed as diverged: P.L. 119-21 raised ARC/PLC reference prices, CRP enrollment continues with 26.8 million acres planned for FY2027, and reconciliation combined SNAP and commodity changes. No action was found on moving nutrition programs to HHS or the Community Eligibility Provision.

11.summary: Seven of 34 tracked recommendations are in effect, including removal of the 2024 Title IX rule, borrowing caps and a new repayment plan, removal of disparate-impact provisions from Title VI rules and Dear Colleague Letter GEN-25-03 of 2025-05-01. Nine are underway, among them program moves to other agencies and the removal of degree requirements. Ten rest on proposals or bills, including the Title VI area studies wind-down, where a 2026-07-01 proposal would remove program regulations while the statute keeps the programs. Two are diverged (indirect cost caps and Impact Aid), and no action was found on six items.

12.summary: Of 34 tracked Department of Energy recommendations, 4 are in effect, including LNG export approvals and the end of energy justice and DEI programs, where the Fourth Circuit vacated a preliminary injunction on 2026-02-06. Seventeen are underway, among them grid supply-chain standards (FERC Order No. 912 and EO 14421), the cancellation of three transmission corridors and a DOE restructuring, where H.R. 7258 passed the House on 2026-06-29 without renaming the department. Four have diverged, including Yucca Mountain, five rest on proposals and no action was found on four items.

13.summary: Of 31 tracked EPA recommendations, 5 are in effect, including the restored 2020 major-source reclassification rule, effective 2026-01-02 with no petition for review found, and relaxed HFC limits. Ten are underway, such as regional haze, Good Neighbor and truck NOx rulemakings, the Title V scope rule of 2026-09-25 and headquarters approval of listed enforcement settlement terms under a memorandum of 2025-12-05. Eleven rest on proposals, including S. 2741, passed by the Senate on 2025-11-19. The grant terminations are blocked, the PFAS designation is diverged, and three items show no action.

14.summary: Of the 67 tracked HHS recommendations, 8 are in effect, including fetal tissue research limits, conscience enforcement, the EMTALA guidance rescission and the inpatient-only list phase-out. Ten are in progress, among them laboratory-developed test oversight, where H.R. 8890 (2026-05-19) would regulate the tests under CLIA and CMS sought comment on CLIA rules on 2026-07-16. Thirty-one are proposed, most of them legislative asks on Medicare, Medicaid and the ACA. Five are blocked, including reference pricing plan designs, stayed by a Maryland court on 2026-07-16. Three diverged and 10 show no action.

15.summary: Of 18 tracked HUD recommendations, five are in effect, including the AFFH repeal, the end of PAVE appraisal policies, climate rollbacks and guidance withdrawals. Three are in progress and six are proposed, among them the noncitizen and work requirement proposals, a rural renovation tax credit bill and public housing disposition, where P.L. 119-101 and HUD Notice PIH 2026-23 expand conversions and ease disposition without new land-sale authority. None is blocked or diverged, and four show no action found, including the FHA statutory package and term-based premiums.

16.summary: Of the 22 tracked Interior recommendations, 8 are in effect, including oil and gas leasing, the 30 by 30 rescission, the Migratory Bird Treaty Act opinion and the settlement transparency order. Nine are in progress, among them coal leasing, Endangered Species Act rules, the two Utah monument reductions of 2026-07-13 and the National Park Service Alaska hunting rule, published 2026-10-19 (91 FR 65985) and effective 2026-11-18. Four are proposed, including BLM headquarters, and no action was found on the BLM law enforcement chain of command.

17.summary: Of the 21 tracked Justice Department recommendations, 3 are in effect, including litigation alignment and the Civil Rights Division refocus. Twelve are in progress, such as immigration prosecutions, cartel cases, where a Deputy Attorney General memorandum of 2025-09-24 expanded Joint Task Force Alpha, Armed Career Criminal Act charging with the restoring bills still in committee, and FBI field realignment. Two are proposed, including a China Initiative restart, where H.R. 1468 was placed on the Union Calendar on 2026-06-15. No action was found on 4 items, including Comstock Act enforcement.

18.summary: Of the 35 tracked Labor recommendations, 4 are in effect, including the rescission of Executive Order 11246, the overtime threshold and the Wagner-Peyser staffing flexibility rule, in effect since 2026-10-19 with no court order found. Nine are in progress, among them disparate-impact and gender-identity enforcement changes, contractor and joint employer rules and OSHA penalty reductions. Thirteen are proposed, including a skills-based contracting bill passed by both chambers, the unemployment insurance data rule effective 2026-11-16 and ESOP valuation under S. 2403, signed 2026-10-15. Two have diverged and seven show no action found.

19.summary: Two of 22 tracked recommendations are in effect: DOT rules restoring the 2019 rule on rules (effective 2026-05-27) and airline enforcement hearings (effective 2026-07-31). Six are underway, including NHTSA's fuel economy rule (effective 2026-11-30) and air traffic control funding in P.L. 119-21. Six rest on proposals or bills, among them Jones Act repeal bills and a FY2027 request cutting FAA research. Ending Essential Air Service is blocked, FRA kept and defended its 2024 crew-size rule (Eleventh Circuit, 2026-08-11), and no action was found on slot allocation or the 1,500-hour rule.

20.summary: Three of sixteen recommendations are in effect: a VA rule restoring the exclusion of abortion services (effective 2026-01-30, under a Federal Circuit petition), the end of most telework announced 2025-02-03, and the separation of the human resources office from the operations, security and preparedness office under their own Assistant Secretaries, described in a VA statement to Congress on 2026-06-24. Three are underway: claims processing, the Oracle health record rollout and scheduling changes. Four rest on proposals, two are blocked (the rating schedule revision and the 2025-08-06 termination of union contracts), and no action was found on four items.

21.summary: Three of 24 tracked recommendations are in effect: NTIA's BEAD restructuring of 2025-06-06, revocation of the 30 by 30 order and the Baldrige transfer announced 2025-12-11. Ten are in progress, including NOAA staffing cuts, export control rules, the connected vehicles ICTS rule and its general authorizations (2025-06-10 onward), termination of 14 advisory committees (notice of 2025-06-10), the ESA harm-definition rescission in force since 2026-09-14 and PTAB changes of 2025-10-20. Four are proposed, among them reorganizing BLS, BEA and Census. Two are blocked, the TikTok divestiture is diverged, and four show no action found.

22.summary: Two of 26 tracked recommendations are in effect: the Corporate Transparency Act exemption for domestic companies (effective 2026-08-14) and withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and the UN climate convention. Nine are underway, including the IRA credit phase-out, permanent 2017 deduction suspensions and the end of the 179D deduction in P.L. 119-21. Five rest on bills, among them the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act passed by the Senate 2026-09-30. P.L. 119-21 kept seven rates, raised the SALT cap and expanded benefit exclusions, classed as diverged on three records; seven show no action found.

23.summary: The chapter presents two opposing positions. Reauthorizing the Export-Import Bank is underway: it operates with a three-member Board (President and Chair confirmed 2025-09-18), approved a loan of up to $10 billion for Project Vault, and has a charter running to 2026-12-31, with S. 3772 and a House draft pending and no markup reported. Abolishing the Bank is classed as diverged, since no step toward abolition was found and the FY2027 request raises EXIM's program budget to $200 million.

24.summary: One of seven tracked recommendations is in effect: the bar on a central bank digital currency (executive order of 2025-01-23 and P.L. 119-101). Fed regulation changes, including withdrawal of climate principles, are underway. Two are proposed: H.R. 5396 on removing the employment goal, reported 2026-06-24, and S. 1646 (introduced 2025-05-07) to report on and time-limit section 13(3) emergency lending. Shrinking the balance sheet is classed as diverged after reserve management purchases began 2025-12-11. No action was found on a Fed mission commission or a statutory monetary rule.

25.summary: Two of thirteen tracked recommendations are in effect: the COVID-era loan fraud cleanup (870,000 suspensions announced 2026-09-14) and the end of SBA's voter registration role after EO 14148 revoked the 2021 voting order. Nine are underway, including SBIC changes in P.L. 119-92 (2026-05-19), the 2025-05-19 lender moratorium, the end of SBA diversity programs, H.R. 3174 on manufacturer loans (passed the House 2025-12-01), SBREFA bills and a FY2027 request cutting SBA 74.7 percent. No action was found on ending direct lending or a medium-sized business class.

26.summary: One of 22 tracked recommendations is in effect: the end of de minimis treatment (EO 14256, EO 14324). Seven are underway, including Section 232 actions on chips and pharmaceuticals, 100 percent expensing in P.L. 119-21 and the Section 805 procurement ban. Three are proposed, among them a 2025-08-25 Defense Department rule barring contracts with Confucius Institute hosts and FDA formula import measures. Reciprocal tariff authority is blocked after Learning Resources v. Trump (2026-02-20); decoupling, tariff repeal, WTO dispute settlement and the 2025-02-05 disbanding of foreign influence units are diverged; five show no action found.

27.summary: One of nineteen tracked recommendations is in effect: the SEC's 2025-03-14 rule ending the Enforcement Director's delegated authority to open formal investigations. Six are underway, including the climate rule rescission proposal of 2026-05-29 and the joint crypto interpretation of 2026-03-23. Eight are proposed, among them the 2026-09-17 Innovation Exemption order and H.R. 9329, ordered reported on 2026-06-30, which would direct a GAO audit of SEC IT spending but sets no two-year investigation limit. Abolishing the CFPB and the PCAOB and FINRA are blocked, and no action was found on ending administrative proceedings.

28.summary: None of ten objectives is in effect. Five are underway: FCC Covered List additions (2025-12-22), spectrum auctions required by P.L. 119-21, satellite and wireline permitting actions, the 2026-08-06 vote repealing the 39 percent national television ownership cap, and proposed rules on Lifeline, high-cost, E-Rate and USF administration, while GAO testified on 2026-07-22 that no national broadband strategy exists. Four are proposed: platform contributions to the Universal Service Fund, children's online safety bills (the House passed the KIDS Act 2026-06-29), a plan against aiding China's AI goals and a clean standards initiative. No FCC action on Section 230 was found.

29.summary: None of three objectives is in effect. The coordination objective is underway through a court ruling: on 2026-06-30 the Supreme Court held in NRSC v. FEC, 6 to 3, that limits on party coordinated expenditures violate the First Amendment, and on 2026-09-03 a district court dismissed related claims as moot; no statute raising contribution limits was found. The FEC has lacked a quorum since 2025-05-01, with two nominees named 2026-02-11 unconfirmed, and no directive limiting DOJ prosecution of FECA violations or having DOJ defend the FEC was found.

30.summary: One of five objectives is complete: Trump v. Slaughter (decided 2026-06-29, 6 to 3) held FTC commissioners removable at will. Four are underway through individual actions: a Joint Labor Task Force created 2025-02-26 whose listed conduct includes collusion on DEI metrics, with warning letters to 42 law firms on 2026-01-30; consent orders barring advertising agencies from coordinating on political viewpoints, with the Meta appeal briefed in the D.C. Circuit; enforcement of the amended COPPA Rule while the House-passed KIDS Act awaits the Senate; and the anticompetitive-regulations inventory under Executive Order 14267.

limits: The headline counts every recommendation tracked so far, 590 today, not every recommendation in the roughly 900-page document. The record began as key objectives from all 30 chapters and is being extended chapter by chapter by reading each chapter in full, so chapters read in full contribute more recommendations than the rest and the figure will move as more are added. Recommendations added in the fuller reading have had one independent review and no red-team pass yet. Foreword items are listed but not counted, because the chapters cover the same ground.
Research and review are done by AI models. Every claim links to its source so that a person can check it, and each objective carries a confidence rating. Errors are possible; corrections are welcome.

Research ran in five passes under a fixed web search budget: a first pass on 2026-10-07, a validation pass on the weakest and in-effect objectives, an in-depth pass that re-researched weak records and added objectives in every chapter, a targeted pass on 2026-10-08 on every objective still rated low confidence, and a primary-source pass the same day that located the deciding official document for records previously rated on secondary sources. Objectives rated medium or low confidence still rest on limited searching, and developments from mid-2026 onward are the most likely to be missing.
A status of "No action found" means the research found none. It is weaker evidence than a documented action, and the reviewer caps its confidence accordingly.
Objectives are not independent. One law, order, or court ruling can count toward several objectives, so the headline share is not a count of separate government actions.
Progress percentages come from a fixed rubric and the average is unweighted. Objectives differ greatly in importance, so the average is a rough gauge only.
Status describes alignment between actions and the document. Officials have said the administration does not follow the document, and many actions have other origins.
Estimated timeframes are inferences from the legal route each objective needs. They are not predictions from any official schedule.

significance.note: Recomputed on 2026-10-18 over the 627 counted recommendations: weighted share from the stored mean scores; the band is the weighted share plus the 5th and 95th percentile deviations of 1,000 bootstrap draws (per-rater scores on 426 records, stored weights for the rest) from their own mean, because clipping the estimated fiscal score at 1 and 3 shifts every draw downward and the uncentered percentiles (kept as band_raw_5_95) fell below the weighted share; quadratic-weighted kappa between raters A and B on 426 records.

trackers.name: Project 2025 Tracker (project2025.observer)
trackers.note: a community tracker organized by agency with three statuses (completed, in progress, not started); it listed 321 objectives with 141 completed and 70 in progress when read on 2026-10-08. It runs advertising and donation links.

trackers.name: Center for Progressive Reform and Governing for Impact executive action tracker
trackers.note: an advocacy-organization tracker; it reported 283 of 532 domestic executive actions initiated or completed as of its February 2026 update.

update_note: The record is refreshed by scheduled runs (Pacific time): a daily run each morning with a news sweep of federal developments, deep checks on a rotation of records and refutation checks on records counted as in effect, and a significance recomputation on Sunday. Every run sends changed objectives to an independent review and logs the changes under Changes. Requests made under Requirements are picked up by the next run.
